what: Extending to depth with a Jerlov model
title: Light in the water column
text: Measurements reach 10 m. go deeper use Jerlov Type II coastal water-type model propagate surface spectrum. luxR’s principal lightweight modeling tier. wavelength uses E(z,λ)=E(z0,λ)exp⁡[−Kd(λ)(z−z0)]E(z,\lambda)=E(z_0,\lambda)\exp[-K_d(\lambda)(z-z_0)]. calculation assumes Kd(λ)K_d(\lambda) constant whole path wavelength bins propagate independently. angular multiple-scattering radiative-transfer solution represent fluorescence, Raman scattering, wavelength redistribution. bundled Jerlov table supported 350–700 nm, input explicitly restricted . universal maximum valid depth: selected water type must remain representative modeled water column.  Spectral narrowing depth clearly visible: red wavelengths attenuated first, leaving blue-green light dominant 20 m. Propagating measured deep spectrum upward uses homogeneous-column assumption reverse. reconstruction can strongly amplify measurement noise interpreted direct surface observation.
code: x0m_Jerlov <- x0m_W[350, 700] lam   <- x0m_Jerlov$lambda Kd_II <- jerlov_Kd("II", lam)  specs <- propagate_spectrum(x0m_Jerlov, Kd_II, from = 0,                             to = c(0, 5, 10, 20, 50)) plot(specs, main = "Depth-propagated spectra — Jerlov Type II")

title: Govardovskii et al. (2000) visual-pigment template. — govardovskii_template
text: template models absorbance sum \(\alpha\)-band (main peak) \(\beta\)-band (short-wavelength shoulder). \(\alpha\)-band follows eqn 1 Govardovskii et al. (2000): $$S_\alpha(\lambda) = \left[   e^{(- x)} + e^{B(b - x)} + e^{C(c - x)} + D \right]^{-1}, \quad x = \frac{\lambda_{\max}}{\lambda}$$ \(\beta\)-band Gaussian (eqn 4): $$S_\beta(\lambda) = A_\beta \exp\!\left[   -\!\left(\frac{\lambda - \lambda_{m\beta}}{w}\right)^2 \right]$$ constants depend chromophore: A1 (eqns 2, 5): \(= 69.7\),     \(= 0.8795 + 0.0459\,e^{-(\lambda_{\max} - 300)^2/11940}\),     \(B = 28\), \(b = 0.922\), \(C = -14.9\), \(c = 1.104\),     \(D = 0.674\); \(A_\beta = 0.26\),     \(\lambda_{m\beta} = 189 + 0.315\,\lambda_{\max}\),     \(w = -40.5 + 0.195\,\lambda_{\max}\). A2 (eqns 6, 8): \(= 62.7 + 1.834\,e^{(\lambda_{\max} - 625)/54.2}\),     \(= 0.875 + 0.0268\,e^{(\lambda_{\max} - 665)/40.7}\),     \(B = 20.85\), \(b = 0.9101\), \(C = -10.37\), \(c = 1.1123\),     \(D = 0.5343\); \(A_\beta = 0.37\),     \(\lambda_{m\beta} = 216.7 + 0.287\,\lambda_{\max}\),     \(w = 317 - 1.149\,\lambda_{\max} + 0.00124\,\lambda_{\max}^2\). full template \(S_\alpha + S_\beta\) normalised maximum, lies within nm \(\lambda_{\max}\) found numerically, returned values depend wavelength grid supplied: grid misses peak returns values 1 rather rescaled. A2 template fitted pigments peaking 444 620 nm, lambda_max outside 440–620 nm rejected A2. A1 accepts 300–700 nm.
